newsitem.title: USA: Dole attacks Clinton, asks why Americans not outraged.
newsitem.headline: Dole attacks Clinton, asks why Americans not outraged.

text.p: Asking angrily "where is the outrage in America?", Republican presidential nominee Bob Dole on Friday unleashed a scathing attack on President Bill Clinton and the national news media.

Dole slammed Clinton for refusing to say he would not pardon individuals connected to the Whitewater affair and tried to tie the president to the so-called Filegate scandal, wherein the White House improperly requested confidential FBI files of Republicans.
"Where is the outrage in America? Where is the outrage in America? Where has the media gone in America?" Dole thundered at a Houston rally.

"We have the president of the United States sitting down there with 900 FBI files, one might be one of yours," he said. "And then we have the president of the United States who won't say he won't pardon somebody who did business with him and might implicate him later on. Where is the outrage in America?"

The scathing rhetoric was the second time in two days Dole has let loose on voters, the White House and the press. Trailing Clinton by double digits in national polls with only 11 days left until the election, Dole said he could not understand why voters seemed willing to overlook Clinton's lack of ethics.
"Somebody told me the press reported that Bob Dole was frustrated. I'm not sure I'm frustrated, but I don't understand," he said.
He once attacked the press, saying reporters were refusing to report stories critical of Clinton.
"We're not going to let the media steal this election," Dole said. "We are going to win this election, the country belongs to the people."
The tough language came as Dole tried to shore up his political base in the South, normally safe Republican territory. Dole must do well in this region if he has any hope of winning the White House.

But Dole and Clinton are locked in a tight race in Texas, which has not voted for a Democratic presidential nominee in 20 years. The state has 32 of the 270 electoral votes needed to win the White House.

A poll released by the Houston Chronicle on Friday showed Dole with a 42 percent to 39 percent lead over Clinton in Texas with the a margin of error of 3.4 percentage points, making the race a toss-up.
But Dole had not been in Texas since June. From Houston, he travels to Dallas and then on to California where his campaign plans to spend millions in the closing days.

Clinton has been hot on Dole's heels during a Southern campaign swing of his own. Clinton attracted massive crowds in Alabama on Thursday and is locked in a tight race with Dole in Florida, another must-win state for the Republican.
